parts.name: Root
parts.description: Holds the collection and the division between the two sides. The `items` prop is the full collection. The `value` prop is the ordered list of the keys at the right side. The left side has the other items.

props.name: items
props.description: The full collection, in the sequence of the left list.

props.name: getKey
props.description: The identity of an item. The default is its `id` field.

props.name: value
props.description:
The keys at the right side, in their sequence. By default it goes in the two directions: use
`bind:value`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The keys at the right side at the start, for when you give no `value`.

props.name: controlledValue
props.description:
Give your own code full control of the state. The component stops to write back to `value`,
and it reports only through `onChange`. Thus the parent can refuse a move: the parent does not
send the new value down. The default is off, because `bind:value` is the usual case and it
needs the write-back.

props.name: onChange
props.description: The component calls it after a move, with the new value and with the items that moved.

props.name: disabledKeys
props.description: The keys of the items that stay at their side.

props.name: name
props.description:
The name of the hidden inputs that hold `value`. Thus the field submits with the form and
needs no other code. The component makes one input for each key, in their sequence. If the
right list is empty, it makes no input, and this is the behavior of a native field with more
than one value.

props.name: moveShortcut
props.description:
Lets `Ctrl`+`Enter` or `Cmd`+`Enter` in a list move its selection to the other list. Each list
has one destination, thus the shortcut needs no direction. It also stays correct when the
layout is a mirror image. Set it to `false` when it is the same as a shortcut of your
application.

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the container element.

props.name: children
props.description: The two lists, the move buttons, and each other element of the layout.

parts.name: Source
parts.description: The left list: each item that is not in `value`. It has `role="listbox"` with more than one selection, and `label` gives it its name.

props.name: label
props.description:
The accessible name of the list. The move buttons and the live region also use it. This is why
it is a string, and not only an `aria-label` value: "Move selected to Selected" is clearer
than "move right", and it stays correct in a right-to-left layout.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of a heading that the user sees, for when the list already has one.

props.name: filter
props.description:
Shows only the items for which this function returns `true`. The input that controls it is
yours, and this prop decides only which items the list shows.

With a filter, "move all" means the rows that the user sees, and not all of the items at that
side. This is what the button appears to promise while a filter is on.

props.name: children
props.description: The content for each item at this side.

props.name: emptyPlaceholder
props.description: The content while the side has no items. If you give none, the component makes nothing.

props.name: virtualizer
props.description: Makes only the rows near the viewport. Read the `virtualizer` prop of `ListBox`.

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the list element.

parts.name: Target
parts.description: The right list, in the sequence of `value`. Thus each item keeps the position where the user moved it.

props.name: label
props.description:
The accessible name of the list. The move buttons and the live region also use it. This is why
it is a string, and not only an `aria-label` value: "Move selected to Selected" is clearer
than "move right", and it stays correct in a right-to-left layout.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of a heading that the user sees, for when the list already has one.

props.name: filter
props.description:
Shows only the items for which this function returns `true`. The input that controls it is
yours, and this prop decides only which items the list shows.

With a filter, "move all" means the rows that the user sees, and not all of the items at that
side. This is what the button appears to promise while a filter is on.

props.name: children
props.description: The content for each item at this side.

props.name: emptyPlaceholder
props.description: The content while the side has no items. If you give none, the component makes nothing.

props.name: virtualizer
props.description: Makes only the rows near the viewport. Read the `virtualizer` prop of `ListBox`.

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the list element.

parts.name: Item
parts.description: One row, at the side where it is now. A double click moves it to the other list. The Enter key changes the selection, as in each listbox with more than one selection.

props.name: item
props.description: The item of this row. The `getKey` function of the Root gives its key.

props.name: textValue
props.description: The text for the typeahead. Without it, the component uses the text content of the row.

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the row.

props.name: children
props.description: The content of the row.

parts.name: MoveSelected
parts.description: Moves the selected items of the opposite list to `to`. It is disabled while that list has no selected item that can move.

props.name: to
props.description: The list that the items go to.

props.name: children
props.description: The content of the button: an arrow, a name, or a different element of your layout.

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the button.

props.name: element
props.description: A bindable reference to the button element.

parts.name: MoveAll
parts.description: Moves each item of the opposite list to `to`, selected or not selected. An item in `disabledKeys` does not move.

props.name: to
props.description: The list that the items go to.

props.name: children
props.description: The content of the button: an arrow, a name, or a different element of your layout.

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the button.

props.name: element
props.description: A bindable reference to the button element.

parts.name: MoveUp
parts.description: Moves the selection of the right list one position toward the start of `value`. It is disabled while nothing is selected there, and while the selection is already at the start.

props.name: children
props.description: The content of the button: an arrow, a name, or a different element of your layout.

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the button.

props.name: element
props.description: A bindable reference to the button element.

parts.name: MoveDown
parts.description: Moves the selection of the right list one position toward the end of `value`. It is disabled while nothing is selected there, and while the selection is already at the end.

props.name: children
props.description: The content of the button: an arrow, a name, or a different element of your layout.

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the button.

props.name: element
props.description: A bindable reference to the button element.

parts.name: Status
parts.description: A hidden live region that announces each move. Without it, a move is silent to a screen reader.

props.name: formatMessage
props.description: Makes the announced message from the move.

dataAttributes.name: data-transfer-list-status
dataAttributes.description: Identifies this live region. Each Button has its own.
